extracted.intended_audience: literary critics, students of literature, and educated readers interested in literary criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and evaluative criteria for literary criticism and the assessment of writers, styles, and religiously-inflected writing; aimed at guiding critics in judging literary significance and artistic quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascertain the master-current
rubrics_metrics.description: To ascertain the master-current in the literature of an epoch, and to distinguish this from all minor currents, is one of the critic's highest functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critic should identify which trend or 'main stream' will most influence the future rather than being distracted by minor or fashionable schools. This is a central task showing the critic's capacity to judge historical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justness of spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: Justness of spirit is one of the most indispensable qualities of the critic's office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercising even-minded, accurate judgment is essential. The critic must avoid prejudice, over-enthusiasm, or pet theories that distort assessment; justness underpins the ability to discern the master-current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid self-will and eccentricity; keep objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic must avoid excesses of self-will and eccentricity and should control his subject-matter and keep himself beautifully objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal idiosyncrasy or self-important bias (illustrated by the example of Carlyle) can lead to mistaking relative or fashionable movements for central ones; maintain objectivity and resist imposing private tastes as universal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge writers by their continuation of central lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how a writer continues or carries forward the most important line(s) of a predecessor's activity (e.g., Heine as the continuator of Goethe's most important line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a writer's significance, look for which aspects of earlier masters they inherit, develop, or subvert; determine whether they carry forward the 'vital' elements that will shape future literature rather than merely following peripheral tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist works from within outwards; originality from individuality
rubrics_metrics.description: As man must live from within outwards, so the artist must work from within outwards; only in this way is it possible to be original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative work should arise from personal inward experience and individuality. Critics should value and seek evidence of inward origin in art when judging originality and artistic worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction as durable artistic quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction is a rare characteristic quality (in soul or talent) that preserves reputation and ultimately corrects popular misapprehensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a writer or work possesses 'distinction' — a subtle, elevating quality that survives immediate fashion and secures lasting influence; it differentiates enduring greatness from temporary popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider setting and outward circumstance as significant
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting and outward circumstance (the external form and fashion of a life or work) are not indifferent: they shape perception and can be a real weakness or strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing works (or biographical subjects), attend to how external milieu, cultural setting, and manner of expression influence meaning and reception; differences in circumstance may be non-essential but are often materially important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudence in recommending devotional/ascetic literature
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lives of the Saints can be dangerous reading for many people; one should not recommend such intense devotional works indiscriminately (especially to young or impressionable readers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics and advisers should judge the suitability of devotional or exemplary texts for particular audiences, warning that ardent but ill-regulated piety induced by such readings may harm health or moral balance; recommend moderation and parental/maternal watchfulness over reading, society, and prayers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate religious expression for grandeur versus modern adaptability
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare religious forms by their outward style and circumstance: Catholicism often presents nobleness, amplitude, and sensuous, imaginative forms; Protestantism may appear provincial, mean, and prosaic but often aligns better with modern social vitality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In assessing religious literature or religious elements in writing, weigh both the aesthetic grandeur (nobleness, imagistic power) and the movement's adaptability or alignment with contemporary spirit; neither grandeur nor modern affinity alone determines lasting value.
